qt: to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (PfE) Subject:

A study published in July 2026 by the European Parliament1 highlights that the West’s main vulnerability in the area of critical raw materials is not so much extraction as refining and midstream processing. It estimates that China controls around 90 % of rare earth refining and 74 % of lithium refining, while European support schemes remain far below those in the US. Meanwhile, French manufacturers face high energy prices, long approval periods and competition from imported products benefiting from foreign subsidies or lower standards. In view of the above: 1.
What specific measures will the Commission propose to boost the capacity of France and the rest of Europe to refine and process critical raw materials?
Does it plan to introduce mandatory criteria for European products in public procurement and support schemes?
How will it ensure that any European stocks remain accessible as a matter of priority to the industries of the Member State that financed them?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026)

The Critical Raw Materials Act1 (CRMA) sets 2030 benchmarks to ensure domestic EU processing capacity to cover 40% of the EU’s annual consumption for each strategic raw material. To achieve the benchmark the Commission has designated in the EU already 93 Strategic Projects, among which 11 located in France with a processing component. Strategic Projects benefit from fast-tracked and streamlined permitting, facilitation of access to finance and support in finding offtakers. The RESourceEU Action Plan2 accelerates the CRMA objectives, establishing a financing hub and measures for dedicated project support through the European Critical Raw Materials Centre. Project support has already delivered results: 17 Strategic Projects have obtained a construction permit, and the EU and Member States mobilised more than EUR 2 billion in public financial support for Strategic Projects. The Industrial Accelerator Act3 proposes mandatory ‘Made in EU’ and low-carbon criteria in public procurement and support schemes for strategic sectors such as aluminum, cement, vehicles and net-zero technologies. The aim is to boost demand for European products, strengthen industrial competitiveness and support decarbonisation, while respecting international obligations. Currently there are no EU level stocks of raw materials. The Commission and several Member States are collaborating on a stockpiling pilot project. A call for expression of interest was opened in September 20264. The pilot will become operational in early 2027, building on Member States and Commission’s capacities. The Critical Raw Materials Centre will afterwards integrate the activities of this pilot when carrying out stockpiling operations.
